author: Pooja Jain
headline: Storyteller | Data Architect | Building Scalable Data & AI Foundations for Enterprise Performance | Linkedin Top Voice 2025,2024 | Open to collaboration
text:
Learn data engineering for free, without any distractions!

Here's all you need to dive in:

📌 Programming languages: Python, Scala and Java

📌 Databases: SQL or NoSQL databases such as Server, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, and Redis are a few popular databases

📌 Data processing & streaming: Apache Kafka, Flink and Spark, Hadoop are popular data processing frameworks used to process and analyse data.

📌 Messaging Platforms: Leverage platforms like Kafka, RabbitMQ, and Pulsar

📌 Data modeling: The process of creating a blueprint for a database, it helps to ensure that the database is designed to meet the needs of the business.

📌 Cloud computing: AWS, Azure, and GCP are the three major cloud computing platforms to deploy data engineering solutions.

📌 Data warehouse and Lake: Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift, Hive, S3, Redshift, and Clickhouse are popular platforms. Explore Normalization, Denormalization, and OLTP vs OLAP systems.

📌 Orchestration: Tools like Airflow, Dagster, Mage, Prefect, Jenkins, and Luigi to schedule and monitor workflows.

📌 Storage Systems: Explore these storage systems like S3, Azure Data Lake, and HDFS.

📌Data quality, data observability, and data governance are the key to keep data accurate, complete, and consistent to monitor and understand data systems.

📌 Data visualization: Tableau, Power BI, Jupyter Notebooks, and Plotty and Looker are some popular tools.

📌 DevOps and data ops: Jenkins, Github Actions, and Terraform to automate and streamline the development and deployment.

➠ Data engineers who want to be successful in 2025-2026 and beyond, get your hands dirty leveraging below projects.

text:
My favorite quotes about data visualization:

1. "Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away." (Antoine de Saint-Exupéry)

2. "Numbers have an important story to tell. They rely on you to give them a clear and convincing voice." (Stephen Few)

3. "Visualization gives you answers to questions you didn’t know you had." (Ben Schneiderman)

4. "The ability to simplify means to eliminate the unnecessary so that the necessary may speak." (Hans Hoffman)

5. "There is no such thing as information overload. There is only bad design." (Edward Tufte)

6. "Data is the new oil? No, data is the new soil." (David McCandless)

7. "Data visualization is the language of decision making. Good charts effectively convey information. Great charts enable, inform, and improve decision making." (Dante Vitagliano)

What is your favorite?
